uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt of USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The valuation date is the date of receipt (2026-06-18). The fair market value is determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USD on the last day of the tax year (2026-03-31). No TDS obligation arises as the amount is below the threshold. Under s.439(8), a bona fide explanation and disclosure of material facts can mitigate penalties.
regimes.reasoning: The receipt of USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH, which taxes such transfers at 30%. The valuation date is determined by Rule 56, which specifies the date of receipt for such assets. The fair market value is determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USD on the last day of the tax year, as per Rule 206. No TDS obligation arises because the amount is below the threshold specified in s.393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)]. Under s.439(8), a bona fide explanation and disclosure of material facts can mitigate penalties.
